contract.words: Collect $3,000 of settled cash within 21 days with no more than 3 hours a week of my own time.

terms.proofCondition: $3,000 of settled cash received in the owner's account within 21 days

strategy.title: No plan within 3 owner hours a week: the six signed audits need 36 owner hours
strategy.why: Six boutique-hotel GMs signed orders at $500 per mystery-guest audit, exactly $3,000, but the record says the owner performs each audit personally at 6 owner hours each: 36 hours, against the 9 the goal allows (3 h/week x 3 weeks). noPlan.decisiveGap: Owner hours: the six signed $500 audits are owner-performed at 6 hours each (36 hours), and each is one 6-hour stay, twice the 3-hour weekly limit, so within the limit no audit can be delivered ($0).
noPlan.resolution: Allow 36 owner hours inside the first 14 days (about 18 h/week for two weeks, each week at least 6 h per audit scheduled) so all six reports are done by day 14; at the card's 7 days to usable cash (paid within 5 days of each report) the $3,000 then settles by day 21. 12 h/week is not enough: the last two audits would finish in week 3 and be paid after day 21. Alternatively the hotels would have to accept a fulfiller other than the owner, which nothing on the record offers.

answers.resolution: Accepted. The relaxation is now 36 hours inside the first 14 days (~18 h/week), so all six reports are done by day 14 and, at the card's 7 days to usable cash, paid by day 21.

answers.finding: MAJOR: The weekly ceiling is 3 h; a 6-hour single-stay audit cannot be done in any one week within it
answers.resolution: Accepted. The offerScope makes each audit one check-in-to-checkout stay of 6 owner hours; within 3 h/week no audit fits, so the reachable amount is $0, and the $500 alternative is removed.

Six boutique hotel general managers signed written orders at $500 per mystery-guest audit (signed orders, 2026-11-22).

reviews.reasons: The stance (NO_PLAN on an OWNER_HOURS constraint) is right: six WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE orders at $500 = exactly $3,000, every chain link established, but the card's offerScope and fulfillmentOwner make the owner the performer at 6 hours per audit, so 6 x 6 = 36 owner hours against a 3 h/week limit. But the two remedies the owner would act on are both wrong on the arithmetic. (1) 'Raise to 36 hours over 21 days (12 h/week) to deliver all six for $3,000': at 12 h/week the owner does 2 audits a week, so audits 5-6 finish in week 3 (days 15-21) and are paid within 5 days of the report, i.e. up to day 26, outside the 21-day window (Brain's own sweep puts usable cash at day 25-43). Carrying $3,000 inside the window needs all six reports by about day 16, i.e. ~36 hours in the first 16 days (~16-18 h/week), or the six hotels agreeing to faster payment. (2) 'Lower the target to $500 (one audit) within 3 h/week' and 'one audit (6 h) fits in 9 hours': the limit is weekly, and a check-in-to-checkout audit is one 6-hour stay that cannot be split across weeks, so a single audit already exceeds 3 h in its week; within the limit as written no audit fits and the reachable amount is $0, not $500.
findings: MAJOR: Remedy 'allow 12 h/week' does not settle $3,000 inside 21 days: last two audits end days 15-21, paid up to 5 days later (day 26). State the hours and schedule that actually settle by day 21 (all six reports by ~day 16) or say faster payment terms are needed.

MAJOR: The weekly ceiling is 3 h; a 6-hour single-stay audit cannot be done in any one week within it, so 'one audit, $500, within 3 h/week' and 'one audit fits in 9 hours' treat a weekly limit as a 21-day pool. Within the limit the reachable amount is $0.
NOTE: decisiveLinks is empty, which is consistent: no link is missing, the binding limit is OWNER_HOURS (a true constraint, with basis captureMechanism).

reviews.reasons: Both MAJOR findings from my review of rev_8774b500b36a_ca87a2 are fixed. NO_PLAN on an OWNER_HOURS constraint is right: 6 WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE orders x $500 = $3,000, all chain links established (Brain: none missing), but each audit is one check-in-to-checkout stay of 6 owner hours (card offerScope/fulfillmentOwner: the owner personally), twice the 3 h weekly limit, so within the limit $0 is reachable. Recomputed remedy: 36 hours finished by day 14 = 18 h/week for two weeks; last report day 14 + the card's 7 days to usable cash (paid within 5 days of the report) = day 21, inside the 21-day window; 12 h/week correctly rejected (audits 5-6 in week 3, paid after day 21). decisiveLinks empty is consistent with a pure constraint.
findings: NOTE: The day-14 schedule lands exactly on day 21, with no slack; any audit slipping a day, or a hotel paying on day 5 plus bank settlement beyond the card's 7 days, misses the window. Finishing by ~day 12 (about 21 h/week) would leave margin.
